text:
ian (sales): Hey team — CovenantBank POC hit a blocker: they need to proxy outbound TLS from their on-prem to our Azure PrivateLink endpoint, but they also require SNI to be preserved for hostname-based routing. Can we confirm supported patterns?

maria (sre-se): Short answer: we support TLS passthrough so SNI is preserved, but it depends on the customer's proxy topology. If the proxy does TLS termination we lose SNI.

ian (sales): They use an enterprise proxy that can do SNI passthrough but needs an explicit allowlist for egress IPs. Do we give fixed egress IPs for Private deployments or per-PE region?

ashley (solutions): For Private (VPC/VNet) deployments we provide either a static NAT egress pool per customer or a range per-region depending on the package. For Hosted PrivateLink we publish a small set of egress IPs per-region for allowlisting.

ben (netops): For Azure PrivateLink specifically: traffic hits our private endpoint (private IP in customer VNet). If the customer's proxy is egressing through their NAT/Gateway, they need to ensure outbound to our model-serving endpoints (port 443) is allowed. No special UDP ports.

david (customer): @ian thanks — can you confirm we don't need to open 80 or any other ports? We block all non-443 traffic outbound by default.

maria (sre-se): Correct — only TCP/443 for model inference and management, and TCP/443 for metrics/callbacks. If you enable streaming or websocket-based SDKs, that still uses TLS over 443.

ian (sales): They also asked about SNI proxy config example. Can we drop a sample config for an SNI transparent proxy (nginx/tcp proxy) that preserves SNI?

ben (netops): Sure — quick nginx stream example we gave them in a previous POC:

```
# /etc/nginx/nginx.conf (stream module)
stream {
    map $ssl_preread_server_name $backend_name {
        host1.example.com backend1;
        host2.example.com backend2;
        default backend_default;
    }

    upstream backend1 { server 10.0.0.10:443; }
    upstream backend2 { server 10.0.0.11:443; }
    upstream backend_default { server 10.0.0.20:443; }

    server {
        listen 443;
        proxy_pass $backend_name;
        ssl_preread on;
        proxy_ssl on;
    }
}
```

ben (netops): That preserves SNI via ssl_preread. If their enterprise appliance doesn't support ssl_preread, they'd need passthrough at L4 or use a dedicated NAT with source IP allowlisting.

ashley (solutions): Also call out that if they're using Azure Application Gateway with TLS termination, Application Gateway will terminate TLS unless configured for passthrough. In many corp setups AGW terminates TLS which breaks SNI-based routing.

ian (sales): Good point. @david can you confirm your proxy type?

david (customer): We're running F5 LTM in front of the internet egress, currently configured for SSL passthrough on egress. We will double-check with netsec.

maria (sre-se): If F5 is passthrough then we're good. Next, for allowlisting: we can provide a signed artifact that lists the egress IPs per-region. Want me to attach that to the ticket?

ian (sales): Yes please. Also they want a short firewall rule snippet to hand to NetSec.

ben (netops): Copy-paste friendly snippet below (they can adapt):

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood inference (Azure PrivateLink) — replace <REGION_IPS> with list
# Protocol: TCP
# Ports: 443
# Destination: <redwood-eip-region-1>, <redwood-eip-region-2>
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 FROM any TO <redwood-eip-region-*>
```

ben (netops): We'll also include the private endpoint IPs if they want to pin at the VNet peering level, but typically allowlisting egress NAT IPs is what NetSec prefers.

david (customer): Got it. One more: does PrivateLink require DNS changes? Our DNS uses split-horizon and we can't easily create mappings in their resolver.

maria (sre-se): Yes — PrivateLink typically relies on private DNS zone mappings so the public hostname resolves to the private endpoint IP inside the VNet. Options:
- They can create Azure Private DNS zones and link them to VNet.
- Or we can give them explicit FQDN-to-IP mapping to add to their resolvers (host file or DNS appliance).

ashley (solutions): For the POC, easiest path is to add a hosts entry on one test VM to validate. For scale they'd want Private DNS. We'll document both approaches in the POC runbook.

ian (sales): Any enterprise blockers we're missing (certs, mTLS, auditing)?

maria (sre-se): Certs: we support standard TLS with SNI. If they require mutual TLS (mTLS) we can accommodate but that's a configuration-heavy path — needs cert exchange and CA pinning. Auditing: we emit connection logs and you can enable audit export to their SIEM via our Private integration.

ben (netops): Also note their egress appliance must preserve the original TLS SNI during handshake for hostname routing to work. If the appliance rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, we need a different architecture.

netops-bot: Ticket #POC-4821 created and assigned to @maria. Details: provide egress IP list, nginx SNI sample, DNS options, and draft firewall snippet.

ian (sales): Thanks bot. @maria can you drop the artifact and I'll send to CovenantBank NetSec?

maria (sre-se): Will do — uploading IP list + short one-page runbook to the ticket by EOD. I'll include the nginx example and an Azure Private DNS how-to.

ian (sales): Awesome. I'll follow up after NetSec responds. :thumbsup:
